text: Your phone rings. Police say you're under arrest. Would you pay $260,000 to make it stop?
One woman in India did. In a single week. There's no such thing as a digital arrest. The officer was a scammer.
So, why do smart people pay?
A parcel in your name, drugs inside, a uniform, a fake police station.
Then, don't hang up and tell no one.
In 2024, Indians lost over $200 million this way.
And then comes the part that empties accounts.
To clear your name, you move your savings to a safe account.
The arrest feels real because you never stop watching.
Now India's Supreme Court says banks that miss red flags should pay victims back.
Real police never arrest you on a video call or ask for money.
Comment, would you have hung up?
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
